title: A regular affine ideal generator gives an exact frame of its ideal module
author: @tomasz
source: Derived local frame formulation of The Stacks Project, Lemma 31.14.2, tag 01WS, proof of (2) => (1), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01WS , together with regularity on all opens as in Section 31.15, Lemma 31.15.7, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C4S . The formal statement uses the registered kernel realization of the ideal module and records the exact image of its frame. This is the local regular-generator argument used in the nodal Cartier-center step for the Philippon alteration frontier; it does not assert the full alteration theorem.

source: Derived affine-atlas formulation of the public Proved principal-cover descent theorem https://prove2.me/theorems/909a009d-1f23-5a0b-8a4b-6a0bb18d473b , together with native projective base change https://prove2.me/theorems/040eceda-1925-55bf-adcc-b73e83e4440a and module-isomorphism transport https://prove2.me/theorems/241df6ce-75a9-54a6-b267-0f889f46d5e6 . The finite principal refinement, its unit-ideal condition and the actual module comparisons are proved in the submitted solution. Applied to the glued nodal Cartier-center module, this supplies global projectivity over an affine base in the Philippon alteration development; projectivity over a nonaffine projective base and the full alteration theorem remain further work.

title: Regular projective alterations of proper integral varieties
author: @tomasz
source: A. J. de Jong, Smoothness, semi-stability and alterations, Publications Mathématiques de l’IHÉS 83 (1996), Theorem 4.1 and Remark 4.2, p. 66, and the definition of alteration in Section 2.20, p. 61: https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1996__83__51_0.pdf . Specialize X to a proper integral variety and the prescribed closed subset to the empty set. Its alteration source is proper over K, so the dense open immersion into the regular projective compactification is an isomorphism. Retain properness, dominance and generic finiteness; omit the normal-crossings divisor conclusion. No smoothness over an imperfect field is asserted.

author: @WillR
source: Elementary finite-set induction. Adjoin weight z: the remainder becomes z times the previous remainder plus (1-z) times the previous nonnegative sum of deficits. The first-order sum of deficits is bounded by the existing number of factors. Induction yields the second factorial count.
